title: Protocol and Border
premise: Silas Voss, a veteran air-crash investigator, has spent three years haunted by the unexplained loss of Flight 4471 — the crash that killed his wife and daughter in row twelve. When the government safe house where he's been hiding is listed for sale online with interior photos revealing classified evidence still taped inside a wall, Silas realizes someone inside the investigation wants him found. Chased by an assassin contracted by three complicit governments and betrayed by the mentor he trusts most, Silas teams up with a disgraced journalist, Mara Okafor, to smuggle the flight data recorder's true readout across borders. In the end, Silas must choose between publishing the truth that will destroy his own reputation as lead investigator — he signed off on the faulty maintenance waiver — or letting the lie stand; he chooses truth, testifying at The Hague, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Dominic Thackeray is the pen name of a former aviation-safety consultant who spent a decade writing incident reports before turning to fiction. He lives near the North Sea coast, where he claims the fog helps him plot.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Silas Voss wakes at 3:14 a.m., as he does every night since Flight 4471, in a government safe house outside Rotterdam. POV: Silas. He reviews the official crash report one more time, finding the same small inconsistency that has kept him awake. Emotional beat: grief calcified into obsession.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: A real-estate alert pings: the safe house is for sale, with interior photos — including the hidden compartment behind the bookshelf where Silas keeps the recovered cockpit voice recorder transcript. POV: Silas. He realizes only six people knew about that room. Emotional beat: the cold shock of realizing safety was always an illusion.

chapters.title: Handler Down
chapters.summary: Silas calls his handler, Director Ansel Brandt, and gets voicemail; by dawn, Brandt's car is fished from a canal. POV: Silas, then a brief cold interlude from the assassin, known only as Corvus, confirming the contract. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Silas flees to Amsterdam and finds investigative journalist Mara Okafor, whose career was destroyed for questioning the 4471 report. POV: Mara. She doesn't trust him — he signed the final report she called fraudulent. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged from mutual damage.

chapters.title: What the Recorder Says
chapters.summary: In a rented basement, they play the CVR transcript Silas copied years ago: the pilots reported hydraulic failure forty minutes before any fault appears in official logs. Someone falsified the maintenance records. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: vindication curdling into horror — his signature is on the cover-up.

chapters.title: Corvus Arrives
chapters.summary: The assassin tracks them through a burner purchase; a rooftop escape across Amsterdam leaves Mara wounded and Silas holding Corvus's dropped phone. POV: alternating Silas and Corvus. Emotional beat: first blood, and the understanding that this killer is methodical, not mad.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Decoding Corvus's phone reveals three governments funded the cover-up because the faulty part was a joint defense-contract component none could afford to ground. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the scale of the enemy becomes clear — this isn't murder, it's policy.

chapters.title: The Mentor
chapters.summary: Silas reaches out to his old instructor, Henrik Dahl, now a respected ICAO official, believing Dahl can authenticate the transcript. POV: Silas. Dahl listens, weeps, and asks for twenty-four hours. Emotional beat: hope rekindled — and the reader senses the trap forming.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bridge
chapters.summary: Dahl sells their location; a night ambush on a Copenhagen bridge kills two bystanders and forces Silas to choose saving the evidence drive or Mara. He saves Mara; Corvus takes the decoy drive. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: guilt compounded — he chose a person over justice, and hates how right it felt.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Fugitives without passports, they cross into Germany hidden in a freight truck, where Mara extracts Silas's confession: he approved the maintenance waiver under pressure and never followed up. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: trust nearly shatters, then holds — she decides the man matters more than the signature.

chapters.title: The Widow of Row Eleven
chapters.summary: They track down another survivor's family — a widow seated one row behind Silas's wife — who received an anonymous settlement and a gag order. POV: Silas. Her testimony gives them a human face and a witness willing to speak. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes purpose shared.

chapters.title: Interpol Closes In
chapters.summary: Silas is formally named a person of interest in Brandt's death; airport cameras multiply. They realize the frame-up is designed to make Silas the scapegoat for everything. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the noose tightening, time running out before The Hague's evidence window closes.

chapters.title: Corvus Unmasked
chapters.summary: Using the assassin's phone, they identify Corvus: a former crash investigator himself, whose own family died in an earlier crash covered by the same consortium — hired to bury what he once sought. POV: Corvus. Emotional beat: the hunter revealed as a mirror of Silas's possible future.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Corvus contacts Silas directly: stop now, live quietly, or die meaninglessly — he shows photos proving he knows every safe house. But he also leaves a thread: the original maintenance ledger, held in a Zurich vault. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation, and the terrifying kinship between them.

chapters.title: Zurich
chapters.summary: A break-in at a private bank vault retrieves the ledger proving the part failed inspection twice before 4471 flew. Alarms split the pair; Silas escapes with pages, Mara with the drive. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: triumph laced with exhaustion — evidence alone won't be enough.

chapters.title: Dahl's Confession
chapters.summary: Cornered by his own conscience and the trio's leverage, Dahl agrees to testify but warns the consortium will kill him within a week either way. POV: Dahl. Emotional beat: a coward's redemption purchased at full price.

chapters.title: Ambush in the Alps
chapters.summary: En route to The Hague, their train is stopped; Corvus boards with orders to end it. Instead, in a locked carriage, Silas offers Corvus the thing money couldn't buy: his name cleared alongside theirs if he testifies. POV: Silas and Corvus. Emotional beat: the climax pivot — loyalty to truth outweighs the contract.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: At The Hague, Silas takes the stand and confesses his own role before presenting the ledger, the CVR transcript, and Dahl's testimony. Governments stall; the consortium's lawyers circle. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the costliest honesty of his life, delivered shaking but unbroken.

chapters.title: Corvus's Price
chapters.summary: Corvus testifies, naming his handlers, and is arrested even as his testimony detonates the consortium. He looks at Silas through the glass and nods once. POV: Corvus. Emotional beat: justice achieved through ruin — victory that feels like mourning.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Warrants cascade across three countries; flights are grounded worldwide as the part is recalled. Mara publishes the full story; Silas watches his own name appear in both columns — perpetrator and whistleblower. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the bitter, necessary wholeness of the whole truth.

chapters.title: The Grave
chapters.summary: Silas visits the memorial wall, finds row twelve, and speaks aloud to his wife and daughter for the first time in three years — telling them everything, including his guilt. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief finally allowed to move.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Months later, Silas and Mara rebuild the investigation unit independently. At 3:14 a.m., he stirs, checks the clock, and — for the first time since the crash — goes back to sleep. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging found not in innocence, but in truth endured together.
